assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: isolated reference image for ONE production 3D game environment model.
Input image 1 is a STYLE AND MATERIAL reference from the approved Drowned Crown storyboard. Extract the cave-rock design language only; do not copy its ship, water, pier, treasure, scenery composition or lighting.
Create ONE complete freestanding broad sea-cavern rock buttress, suitable for a premium Crash Bandicoot 4 pirate-level environment. It is an asymmetrical joined mass of five or six large overlapping rock lobes, approximately twice as wide as tall and substantial in depth. A few thick uneven horizontal shelves and softly tapering shoulders, one dominant tall curved mass on the right, lower rounded ledges on the left, deep deliberate cracks separating the big forms. Broad QUIET sculpted faces, gently rounded chisel bevels, purposeful angular plane changes, only a few selected chips. Blue-grey and lavender-slate hand-painted albedo with restrained lighter edge colour and slightly warmer dry facets. Sparse muted moss only on two small ledges.
Show the whole object in front three-quarter view with a small amount of its right side and top visible. Complete irregular silhouette with a generous white margin, no rectangular pedestal or flat scene background attached to the model. Closed thick rocky back is inferred; this is solid geology, not a thin sheet. Visually low-poly-compatible but beautifully sculpted and textured; sharp readable designed shapes, not raw faceted triangulation.
Neutral diffuse studio illumination for image-to-3D extraction, no blue environmental lighting, amber light, cast shadow or glow baked into the asset. Pure white background, not transparent. No scene, floor, water, sky, buildings, wood, people, text, border, labels or collage. Avoid realistic gritty stone micro-noise, tiny rippled erosion wrinkles, column grids, giant spikes, repeated bands, repeating tile texture and glossy plastic. Landscape image at highest available native quality.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: isolated reference for ONE production 3D cave-ceiling model.
Input image 1 is the approved cave-rock MATERIAL AND SHAPE style reference. Input image 2 is the approved moonpool STORYBOARD for the skylight idea only. Do not reproduce either whole scene.
Create one broad thick irregular horizontal STONE ROOF RING surrounding a large natural oval skylight hole. This is a solid rocky ceiling module, like the eroded roof of a sea cavern with a hole worn through it. Its outer footprint is roughly 26 metres wide by 22 deep, thickness around 6 metres, opening about 11 by 8 metres. The opening goes completely THROUGH the rock; pure white background is clearly visible through the large oval hole. No glass, opaque filling or picture in the hole.
View it from BELOW in a front three-quarter angle looking upward, showing the complete outer silhouette, sculpted underside, interior lip of the opening and a little of one outer side. The ring is horizontal, not a vertical doorway. Uneven rounded joined rock lobes, broad bevelled slate planes, several short tapered stalactites on the underside, asymmetrical heavier mass at one end. Only a few long designed cracks and restrained chips, quiet broad planes. Blue-grey/lavender hand-painted stone matching image 1, dry muted warm edges, no gritty realism or repeated erosion wrinkles. A little green moss on the upper rim only.
Premium Crash Bandicoot 4 pirate-environment sculpture and painted PBR material quality. Neutral soft studio light, no directional light or glow baked in. Pure WHITE background and generous margin around the entire model. No floor, walls descending to a floor, scenery, ship, water, sky image, sunbeam, vegetation hanging below, people, text, labels, grid, border or pedestal. One coherent closed-volume rocky annulus; the hole and outer silhouette are exceptionally clear. Highest available native landscape resolution.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: isolated MATERIAL STYLE reference for retexturing an existing 3D pirate-galleon hull.
Input image 1 is the OBJECT AND SHAPE reference: preserve its long curved hull, raised stern at left, tapered bow at right, horizontal strakes, open top, exposed inner ribs, gunports and broad carved ornament positions. Input image 2 is the approved Crash 4-inspired STYLE AND PALETTE reference only.
Create one new, beautifully rendered view of this same hull with premium Crash Bandicoot 4 pirate-level materials. Warm honey-orange oak and rich reddish chestnut planks with broad, deliberately painted grain. A restrained deep burgundy/navy band at the upper gunwale, soft dark brown seams, clean readable warm brass and antique-gold maritime carvings. Thick sculpted-looking edges and strong large material shapes; fewer noisy scratches and salt streaks. The lower hull remains warm mid-brown with subtle cool damp accents, NOT black, grey, dirty or desaturated. The inner planking is also warm and readable. High-quality stylized PBR with matte wood, soft roughness variation and tasteful gold highlights. Bright diffuse neutral studio light, no dramatic directional lighting or shadows baked into the material.
Keep the reference hull design recognisable and material boundaries aligned to the existing geometry; this is a material/style guide, not a new ship layout. Show the entire freestanding hull in the same three-quarter orientation, generous margin, no cropping. Pure white background. No masts, sails, buildings, deck clutter, people, water, scenery, text, labels, logo, border or pedestal. Avoid photographic micro-grain, grey weathering, black tar over most surfaces, gritty salt noise, high-gloss plastic and dense tiny ornament that overwhelms the wood. One full landscape reference at the highest native resolution available.

Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production diffuse/albedo texture atlas for individual wooden deck boards in a 3D pirate platformer.
Primary request: create a quiet, premium hand-painted oak plank-face atlas in the Crash Bandicoot 4 pirate environment style shown in the reference. The reference is a STYLE AND WOOD-COLOR guide only; do not render its scene, lighting or perspective.
Composition: flat orthographic texture image, wide 16:9 canvas, exactly SIX equal-height horizontal bands stacked edge-to-edge. Each band is the face of ONE single long continuous wooden board spanning the full image width. Six rectangular swatches, all with grain running left-to-right. No end-to-end board joints inside any band. No white gutters, borders, text, labels or numbers. Keep narrow dark separations at the six band boundaries only.
Materials: warm mid-value honey/ochre oak, a little russet and muted dusty tan variation between the six boards. Broad restrained carved grain strokes, occasional shallow chips, softly painted edge wear. Give each board a different sparse grain arrangement, at most one small knot on a few boards, only a few small dull iron nail heads near the ends. Most surface area must be calm wood color. Large readable forms suitable for a colorful stylized game, not realistic timber photography.
Lighting: neutral evenly lit albedo, no directional shadows, no lantern glow, no sun highlights, no ambient occlusion gradient, no glossy reflections.
Constraints: precisely six horizontal board-face swatches; straight rectangular UV regions; same proportions across rows. Do not make a tiled floor pattern. Do not add objects, rope, hardware beyond sparse nails, cracks across the entire atlas, or perspective. Avoid dense fine grain, gritty noise, severe black grooves and high-frequency scratches.
assets.reason: The user required existing Meshy boards with their original assets. The pending imagegen call finished but its image was discarded, and the associated code changes were reverted. Not copied to public assets or used by the game.

review: Native-resolution Imagegen output inspection, then 3840x2160 model and player-view review. No image resizing or tiling.
